A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NAVER and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Sections 6–10. Their matching framework and complete experimental material support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection and segmentation results, component ablations, runtime and failure analyses, and supplementary sensitivity studies.

after.justification: v2 reports original detection and segmentation results, revised component ablations, efficiency measurements, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The five-state automaton, transitions, ProbLog-to-Scallop reasoning, verification procedure, retry mechanism, and prompts remain unchanged. Florence2-L was already tested as an interchangeable detector in v1; v2 changes its experimental prominence.

E1.justification: Both versions cover referring-expression detection and segmentation using RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg, Ref-Adv, and RefCLEF. The revised query-length analysis uses another already-covered dataset without expanding overall task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: SimVG is added to v2's detection comparisons and grounding-model analysis, while ReCLIP disappears from the detection comparison. The principal compositional comparators and segmentation baseline sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Detection comparisons and ablations switch from IoU to accuracy, with IoU retained in v2 Table 10. The main starred configuration changes from GroundingDINO-B/InternVL2 to Florence2-L/InternVL2; the former configuration remains as the double-dagger group. Figure 4 switches from RefCOCOg IoU to RefCOCO accuracy and changes its query-length bins.

E4.justification: v1's separate automaton/logic and Answerer/logic ablations become v2's joint Table 7. It adds all-disabled and logic-only controls, omits the previous automaton-plus-Answerer configuration without logic, and extends Answerer comparisons to four datasets. SimVG extends detector sensitivity testing, and the query-length analysis is revised; the self-correction analysis remains unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and sample-averaged runtimes without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Detection results are extensively added or replaced under revised metrics and configurations. v1's GroundingDINO-based NAVER starred IoUs reappear unchanged as the double-dagger row in v2 Table 10. However, under the retained GLIP/BLIP configuration, RefCOCOg IoU changes from 61.2 to 59.2 for NAVER and from 60.6 to 63.6 for ViperGPT, reversing their ranking. Ablation results, LLM timings, and query-length curves also change; results in Tables 3–6 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal DFA definition, transition rules in Table 1, and mathematical description of probabilistic grounding remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: explicit probabilistic logic, a self-correcting automaton, interpretable grounding, and claimed state-of-the-art performance. Revised experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 extends the Python-generation bottleneck explanation from HYDRA to ViperGPT, removes v1's discussion attributing baseline behavior to training overlap and YOLO's reasoning limitations, and adds configuration-wide superiority claims in supplementary Section 6. The stated limitation concerning LLM code-generation capability remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 updates the stated detector to Florence2-L, and v2 Table 10 explicitly documents three shared-backbone comparison groups. Table 2 also revises the reported pretrained detectors' training-data coverage to include RefCOCOg. Hardware, Scallop conversion, retry cap, prompt templates, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds SimVG and removes ReCLIP, with additional comparator citations in the introduction. The central positioning against existing end-to-end and compositional methods remains unchanged; most citation-number changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in experimental discussion and the supplementary roadmap. Answerer discussion is incorporated into Section 4.4, supplementary Section 6 becomes additional quantitative comparison, and FSA terminology is standardized to DFA. The broader narrative and method exposition remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Experimental displays are substantially reorganized: Table 7 combines three ablation factors, Table 8 replaces paired rows with side-by-side performance columns, and supplementary Table 10 becomes a wide accuracy/IoU comparison replacing the former Answerer table. Figures 3 and 4 expand across both columns, and Figure 4 changes its axes and plot. The overview diagrams remain intact.

improvement.justification: v2's additional ablation controls and explicit metric/backbone comparisons improve assessability. However, retained-setting RefCOCOg IoUs change from NAVER/ViperGPT 61.2/60.6 to 59.2/63.6, contradicting v2 Section 6's configuration-wide superiority claim. Figure 4 also introduces overlapping final bins labeled 12–15 and 13+. These benefits and new reporting inconsistencies leave the net effect on overall quality uncertain.
